name: Hotel Paracas
positioning: Hotel Paracas, a Luxury Collection Resort: a beachfront resort facing Paracas National Reserve, three hours south of Lima, with a private dock, terraced rooms and a spa
best_for: Nature lovers who want yacht trips to see sea lions and penguins at the Ballestas Islands
Families who want a kids' program and a family pool
Travelers who want a terrace with sea or garden views

facts.text: The resort is three hours south of Lima, facing Paracas National Reserve.
The resort has a private dock.
Peruvian architect Bernardo Fort-Brescia designed the resort, built amid the ruins of the original Hotel Paracas, which crumbled in a 2007 earthquake.
The resort's two-story white bungalows incorporate bamboo in their design.
Every room and suite has a furnished terrace with sea or garden views.
Bathrooms have a full tub with signature bath products and a rainfall showerhead.
Aqu Spa is a 547-square-meter spa offering beauty treatments and wellness rituals.
There are two heated pools: the main pool facing the Bar Lounge and the Koni Family Pool next to the playground.
Catamaran and kayak rental are complimentary at the watersports desk.
Koni Camp is a children's program inspired by the pre-Inca Paracas culture.
Chalana Restaurant, at the hotel's private dock, serves fish and seafood.
The hotel holds the Biosphere Sustainable certification.

highlights.text: Guests can watch marine wildlife and sunsets from a 52-foot luxury yacht and visit the Ballestas Islands sanctuary for an up-close look at sea lions and penguins.
The Plunge Pool Suite has its own plunge pool, with views of the family pool, resort activities and the ocean.
Rooms feature bamboo wall coverings, geometric textiles and other pre-Incan decor.
The concierges are bilingual, certified destination experts who wear the Les Clefs d'Or insignia.
The concierge suggests desert excursions in private SUVs that end with a Peruvian picnic at sunset.

considerations.text: The resort is three hours south of Lima, so plan how you will get there.
Paracas is also the name of a strong wind that occasionally produces sand storms.
Nautical sport availability depends on weather and is restricted for children 5 and younger.
